content.text: A new project has been created here, which will be the one going forward:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify
What is the definition of "done" for this ticket?
Are we there with the creation of this new repo?
Do we need to demonstrate completion of a specific set of requirements?
Possibly the Phase-2 requirements from this list:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/Design+-+Import+-+Export#Design-Import-Export-VerificationTool
To say we've completed the initial integration of the two tools I think we would still need to do at least the following:
create a fuller README with instructions on use
bring over the more robust logging feature of the other tool and integrate that here
rename the current CSV summary feature as something other than "log"
migrate other advanced features from the other tool?
Thanks,
Numbers 1,2 and 3 are clear.
Can you or
elaborate on number 4?
4 was really just an invitation to Bethany or you to say if there were other features that we ought to try to move over.
Since I am less familiar with
's tool's bells and whistles, I will defer to her to detail what must be migrated over... a specific list would be helpful.
Following up on

's question from the call earlier, I see now the implementation I described of using "prefer header = minimal" to skip server managed triples was in fact implemented only in my mind, so something along those lines will need to be done to make this work for import.  It is complicated, though, because the triples on disk will include the server-managed ones, and so we'll need to work around that (perhaps something like checking if the minimal triples coming from Fedora are a subset of what is on disk).
There are also a couple typo bugs on the import side, so clearly that part hasn't been tested.
I also think
is a blocker for proper functioning of the verification tooling on import operations.
Josh-
We do that kind of filtering in the import utility now:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/blob/master/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/importexport/importer/Importer.java#L270-L278

But I'm not thrilled with that approach of filtering out a laundry-list of predicates and types.  Checking whether the minimal triples are a subset of the standard triples sounds like a cleaner approach.

The subset option is easy to implement, but there is some danger of false positive verification, if for example some number of non-server-managed triples didn't successfully import, then the graph of triples in Fedora could still be a subset of the graph on disk – though presumably the import-export tooling would have caught such an error because Fedora would (I'm guessing) complain that it could not accept all triples in the submitted graph.

An alternative occurred to me that one could make two requests to Fedora, once for minimal triples and once for the full set, and then diff the two graphs to get the set of server-managed triples.  Those server managed triples could then be stripped out from a graph of the triples on disk one by one (with some logic for matching subject/predicate – the subject, however, being relative depending on whether the base repository or port has changed) to arrive at the non-server managed triples for the graph on disk.
All of this will be unnecessary once the import tooling can set server managed triples.
I plan on working on adding in logging capabilities this week.
Just created this PR for adding logging to the verification tool.
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify/pull/7
It might need to be tweaked, but I wanted to get it in so that it's available for the sprint starting next week.
Fully resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify/commit/30ac7a88d0ba3ab8f1cedb38b9a909f1f1939d46
This task is to consolidate the following two (python) verification tools:
https://github.com/bseeger/fcrepo-sample-dataset-tests
, and
https://github.com/jwestgard/fcrepo-import-export-verify
The combined tool is now
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify
, and the README has been expanded.
The main task remaining is to migrate the logging feature from the fcrepo-sample-dataset-tests to the new combined tool.

A new project has been created here, which will be the one going forward:

https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify

What is the definition of "done" for this ticket?

  • Are we there with the creation of this new repo?
  • Do we need to demonstrate completion of a specific set of requirements?
    • Possibly the Phase-2 requirements from this list: https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/Design+-+Import+-+Export#Design-Import-Export-VerificationTool

To say we've completed the initial integration of the two tools I think we would still need to do at least the following:

  1. create a fuller README with instructions on use
  2. bring over the more robust logging feature of the other tool and integrate that here
  3. rename the current CSV summary feature as something other than "log"
  4. migrate other advanced features from the other tool?

Thanks, Joshua Allan Westgard.
Numbers 1,2 and 3 are clear.
Can you or Bethany Seeger elaborate on number 4?
4 was really just an invitation to Bethany or you to say if there were other features that we ought to try to move over.
Since I am less familiar with Bethany Seeger's tool's bells and whistles, I will defer to her to detail what must be migrated over... a specific list would be helpful.

Following up on Esmé Cowles's question from the call earlier, I see now the implementation I described of using "prefer header = minimal" to skip server managed triples was in fact implemented only in my mind, so something along those lines will need to be done to make this work for import. It is complicated, though, because the triples on disk will include the server-managed ones, and so we'll need to work around that (perhaps something like checking if the minimal triples coming from Fedora are a subset of what is on disk).

There are also a couple typo bugs on the import side, so clearly that part hasn't been tested.

I also think FCREPO-2240 Closed is a blocker for proper functioning of the verification tooling on import operations.

Josh-

We do that kind of filtering in the import utility now:

https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/blob/master/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/importexport/importer/Importer.java#L270-L278

An alternative occurred to me that one could make two requests to Fedora, once for minimal triples and once for the full set, and then diff the two graphs to get the set of server-managed triples. Those server managed triples could then be stripped out from a graph of the triples on disk one by one (with some logic for matching subject/predicate – the subject, however, being relative depending on whether the base repository or port has changed) to arrive at the non-server managed triples for the graph on disk.

All of this will be unnecessary once the import tooling can set server managed triples.
I plan on working on adding in logging capabilities this week.

Just created this PR for adding logging to the verification tool.

https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify/pull/7

It might need to be tweaked, but I wanted to get it in so that it's available for the sprint starting next week.
